transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

That 'Er03' code isn't in our standard database for AEG hobs, but given that your pasta water boiled over right before it happened, the most likely cause is spillage tracking under the glass or into the control panel. This often triggers a safety shutdown to prevent electrical faults. Please isolate the hob at the wall (switch off the fused spur or circuit breaker) for about 15 minutes to allow any moisture to evaporate and the electronics to reset. Once you turn it back on, check if the control surface is completely dry. Does the error appear immediately upon switching it on, or only when you try to select a cooking zone?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I already wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes, and it works now. It was starchy water across the slider. Is it fine to keep using it?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. To prevent this happening again, try to keep spills off the slider and control panel as much as possible, and if you do get a spillage, wipe it immediately with a dry cloth. If the error returns without any spillages nearby, then we would need to look at internal components, but for now, you are good to go.

candidates: Spillage tracking causing a safety shutdown or short circuit (high)
Control panel moisture sensor triggering an error (medium)

The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
